title: B. Flip the Bit (Easy Version)
statement:
This is the easy version of the problem. The difference between the versions is that in this version, there is exactly one special index ($$k=1$$). You can hack only if you solved all versions of this problem.

You are given a binary array $$a$$ of length $$n$$ and $$k$$ special indices $$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_k$$ ($$1 $\leq p_i \leq n$$$). It is given that the values $$a_i$$ of all elements at special indices are the same (i. e., $$a_{p_1} = a_{p_2} = \ldots = a_{p_k}$$).

In one operation, you can choose a range $$[l, r]$$ ($$1 $\leq l \leq r \leq n$$$) such that the range contains at least one special index ($$l $\leq p_i \leq r$$$) and flip all bits $$a_j$$ for $$l $\leq j \leq r$$$. Flipping a bit changes $$0$$ to $$1$$ and $$1$$ to $$0$$.

Let $$x$$ denote the value at special indices before any operations are applied . Find the minimum number of operations required to make all elements of the array equal to $$x$$.

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains two integers $$n$$ and $$k$$ ($$1 $\leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$; $$k=1$$) — the length of the array and the number of special indices.

The second line contains $$n$$ integers $$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$ ($$0 $\leq a_i \leq 1$$$) — the elements of the array.

The third line contains $$k$$ integers $$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_k$$ ($$1 $\leq p_1  \lt  p_2  \lt  \ldots  \lt  p_k \leq n$$$) — the special indices. It is guaranteed that $$a_{p_1} = a_{p_2} = \ldots = a_{p_k}$$.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $$n$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$2 $\cdot 10^5$$$.

For each test case, output a single integer — the minimum number of operations required.

For the first test case, you can choose the range $$[1, 3]$$ and flip all the bits to get $$[1, 0, 1]$$. Then you can choose the range $$[2, 2]$$ and flip the second bit to get $$[1, 1, 1]$$.

For the second test case, all the bits already match the value at the special index. You do not need any operations.
